quotes: We performed a rigorous test of whether leading machine-learning algorithms (transformers) learn like brains.
the transformers spontaneously developed the same structure as newborn visual systems
it is unnecessary to postulate a central role for genes in guiding the organization of visual systems
Unlike CNNs, transformers are generic learners without hardcoded domain-specific priors.
did not use spatiotemporal retinal waves (the models were trained on static images)
hierarchical & retinotopic architectures (i.e., gradually increasing receptive field sizes across layers)
we did not shuffle the images and passed the images sequentially to the model during training
We maintained the original sequence of frames across all epochs, without shuffling.
both the temporal windows and the images within each window were randomly shuffled in each epoch
Each vision transformer model was trained using three different seeds
Overall, transformers appear to be accurate models for predicting the learning outcomes of brains.
The output is then normalized before visualizing
We speculate that giving transformers a prenatal developmental phase will make them more brain-like
without genes to instruct development in any way
no convolutional layers were used to create image patches
Space-time adaptation to retinal waves causes transformers to develop larger receptive fields across layers
